headline: A new federal law removes the time limit for child victims of human trafficking or certain federal sex offenses to file civil lawsuits for damages.
what_it_does: The law eliminates the statute of limitations for a minor who was a victim of a human trafficking offense or a federal sex offense. A statute of limitations is a deadline for filing a lawsuit. Under this law, a victim who was a minor can file a civil action to recover damages no matter how much time has passed.

who_it_affects.group: Minors who were victims of human trafficking or federal sex offenses
who_it_affects.how: They can file civil lawsuits to recover damages without the usual filing deadline.

who_it_affects.group: Adults who were abused as children
who_it_affects.how: Those who were minor victims of these offenses can seek civil damages even if the usual deadline has passed.

who_it_affects.group: People and organizations who could be sued for these offenses
who_it_affects.how: They may face civil claims that are filed long after the events occurred, because the usual deadline no longer applies.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted September 16, 2022. The official summary does not describe a separate effective date.
